Adaptive algorithms

Adaptive DSP equalization for optical links

A study of blind equalizers for polarization-mixed optical signals, including a variable-momentum CMA route that converged up to eight times faster.

At a glance

Make the equalizer respond faster without giving up recovery quality.

CMAVM-CMALMSOptical links
Problem

Polarization-mode dispersion, phase noise, carrier-frequency offset, and additive noise rotate and smear received constellations. Standard constant-modulus adaptation is robust but slow, and higher-order modulation complicates its single-radius assumption.

Algorithms compared

The study compares standard CMA with momentum, variable-momentum, second-moment, L-BFGS, and multi-modulus variants across SNR, group delay, and filter-tap settings. Variable momentum changes optimizer behaviour as convergence approaches.

Joint equalization & carrier correction

A decision-directed LMS formulation estimates equalizer taps and carrier-frequency offset together, keeping the final CFO estimate within five percent of the simulated offset in tested conditions.

Takeaway

No equalizer is universally best: convergence speed, steady-state error, block-processing cost, and modulation order all matter. The variable-momentum route offered a practical improvement because its behaviour changed over the course of adaptation.
